title: CISSP Domains (CBK)
description: The eight domains defined by ISC² that make up the CISSP Common Body of Knowledge.

title: Domain 1 - Security and Risk Management
description: Covers foundational security concepts, risk management, governance, compliance, and ethics.

title: Domain 2 - Asset Security
description: Covers the classification, ownership, and protection of information and physical assets.

title: Domain 3 - Security Architecture and Engineering
description: Covers secure design principles, security models, cryptography, and physical security.

title: Domain 4 - Communication and Network Security
description: Covers secure network architecture, transmission methods, and communication protocols.

title: Domain 5 - Identity and Access Management
description: Covers identification, authentication, authorization, and access control mechanisms.

title: Domain 6 - Security Assessment and Testing
description: Covers security assessments, penetration testing, audits, and logging and monitoring.

title: Domain 7 - Security Operations
description: Covers incident response, investigations, disaster recovery, and operational security.

title: Domain 8 - Software Development Security
description: Covers secure coding practices, software development lifecycle security, and application security.

title: Security and Risk Management Frameworks
description: Structured models and standards used to guide security and risk management practices.

title: Framework Types
description: The different categories or classifications of security and risk management frameworks.

title: NIST
synonyms: National Institute of Standards and Technology
description: US federal agency that publishes widely adopted cybersecurity and risk management frameworks.

title: ISO/IEC
description: International standards body publishing security management standards such as the ISO/IEC 27000 series.

title: NIST CSF 2.0
description: A voluntary outcome-based cybersecurity framework published by NIST.

title: ISO 27001 (ISMS)
description: International standard specifying requirements for an Information Security Management System (ISMS), certifiable by accredited bodies.

title: SP 800-39
description: A NIST Special Publication that defines an information security risk management process.

title: ISO 27005
description: An ISO/IEC standard defining an information security risk management process.

title: SP 800-37 (RMF)
description: A NIST Special Publication defining the Risk Management Framework, a system authorization lifecycle.

title: SP 800-30 Rev 1
description: A NIST Special Publication defining a risk assessment methodology.

title: Does not define a risk assessment methodology
synonyms: Does not prescribe a risk assessment methodology

title: SP 800-53
description: NIST Special Publication 800-53, a catalog of security and privacy controls for U.S. federal information systems.

title: ISO 27002
description: ISO/IEC 27002, a code of practice that catalogs information security controls.

title: ISO 27003
description: ISMS implementation guidance standard.

title: No dedicated NIST publication
synonyms: Absence of a specific NIST publication
Not covered by a standalone NIST SP
No specific NIST SP for ISMS implementation
description: NIST does not publish a document specifically dedicated to ISMS implementation guidance.

title: Implicitly covers ISMS implementation guidance
synonyms: ISMS guidance is implicit in RMF
description: SP 800-37 (RMF) implicitly contains the ISMS implementation guidance dimension rather than addressing it in a separate publication.

title: SP 800-55
description: NIST publication on security measurement and metrics.

title: ISO 27004
description: ISO/IEC standard on information security management measurement and metrics.

title: NIST IR 8286
description: NIST publication on integrating cybersecurity and enterprise risk management.

title: ISO 31000
description: ISO standard providing principles and guidelines for enterprise risk management.

title: ISO 27000
description: ISO/IEC standard providing the vocabulary and overview for the ISMS family of standards.

title: Core
description: Component of NIST CSF 2.0 that organizes cybersecurity outcomes into functions.

title: Tiers
description: Component of NIST CSF 2.0 describing the rigor of cybersecurity risk management practices.

title: Profiles
description: Component of NIST CSF 2.0 used to measure the gap between current and desired cybersecurity states.

title: Govern (GV)
description: First function of the CSF Core, covering cybersecurity governance.

title: Identify (ID)
description: CSF Core function focused on understanding assets, risks, and context.

title: Protect (PR)
description: CSF Core function covering safeguards to ensure delivery of critical services.

title: Detect (DE)
description: CSF Core function for identifying cybersecurity events in a timely manner.

title: Respond (RS)
description: CSF Core function covering actions taken upon detection of a cybersecurity incident.

title: Recover (RC)
description: CSF Core function focused on restoring capabilities or services impaired by an incident.

title: Tier 1 - Partial
description: Lowest CSF maturity tier with ad hoc and reactive risk management practices.

title: Tier 2 - Risk-Informed
description: CSF maturity tier where risk management practices are approved by management but not organization-wide.

title: Tier 3 - Repeatable
description: CSF maturity tier with formally approved, organization-wide risk management practices.

title: Tier 4 - Adaptive
description: Highest CSF maturity tier with continuous improvement based on lessons learned and predictive indicators.

title: Current Profile
description: Profile representing the organization's current state against CSF Core functions and categories.

title: Target Profile
description: Profile representing the desired cybersecurity state, aligned with business objectives and risk appetite.

title: Organizational Context (GV.OC)
description: Establishing the organization's mission, stakeholders, and external dependencies as input to cybersecurity governance.

title: Risk Management Strategy (GV.RM)
description: Organization-wide strategy defining how cybersecurity risk is identified, prioritized, and treated.

title: Risk Appetite and Tolerance
description: The level of risk the organization is willing to accept (appetite) and the acceptable deviation from it (tolerance).

title: ERM Integration
description: Embedding cybersecurity risk into the broader Enterprise Risk Management program.

title: Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management (GV.SC)
description: Managing cybersecurity risk that arises from suppliers, vendors, and third-party dependencies.

title: Cybersecurity Culture
description: The shared values, behaviors, and awareness that shape how an organization treats cybersecurity.

title: Added in NIST CSF v2.0 as cross-cutting function
description: GOVERN is the function newly introduced in NIST CSF v2.0 and applies across all other functions.

title: Improvement category moved from IDENTIFY in v2.0
description: Continuous improvement was previously under IDENTIFY in CSF v1.x and was relocated to GOVERN in v2.0.

title: Asset Management (ID.AM)
synonyms: Inventory of hardware software data and people
description: Cataloging hardware, software, data, and personnel assets that the organization must protect.

title: Critical Business Process Mapping
description: Identifying and mapping the business processes whose disruption would most affect the organization.

title: Risk Assessment (RA) (ID.RA)
description: Evaluating the likelihood and impact of cybersecurity risks to the organization.

title: Threat and Vulnerability Identification
description: Identifying threats facing the organization and vulnerabilities in its assets and processes.

title: Identity Management, Authentication, and Access Control (PR.AA)
description: NIST CSF PROTECT category covering access control, identity, and authentication.

title: Awareness and Training (PR.AT)
description: Educating personnel on cybersecurity responsibilities, threats, and safe behaviors.

title: Data Security (PR.DS)
description: Protecting data confidentiality, integrity, and availability via mechanisms such as encryption and DLP.

title: Protective Processes and Procedures
description: Documented processes and procedures used to protect systems and data.

title: Maintenance
description: Performing maintenance and repair of systems consistent with security policies.

title: Platform Security (PR.PS)
description: Hardening and securing the technology platforms that host applications and data.

title: Continuous Monitoring (DE.CM)
description: Ongoing observation of systems and networks to detect cybersecurity events.

title: Adverse Event Analysis (DE.AE)
description: Analyzing anomalies and events to determine whether they represent security incidents.

title: Detection Processes
description: Processes and technology (SIEM, IDS/IPS, SOC) that implement the detection capability.

title: Dwell time is a critical performance indicator
description: The gap between compromise and detection is a critical KPI for measuring detection effectiveness.

title: Response Planning
description: Pre-defined plans that govern how the organization responds to incidents.

title: Incident Response Reporting and Communication (RS.CO)
description: Internal and external communications during an incident, including regulatory notification obligations.

title: Forensic Analysis
description: Investigation of an incident's scope, cause, and impact through forensic techniques.

title: Mitigation (RS.MI)
description: Actions taken to contain an incident and reduce its impact.

title: Post-Incident Improvement
description: Updating response capabilities based on lessons learned from prior incidents.

title: Incident Recovery Plan Execution (RC.RP)
description: Pre-defined plans for restoring systems and services after an incident.

title: Plan Improvement from Lessons Learned
description: Updating recovery plans based on lessons learned from incidents and exercises.

title: Incident Recovery Communication (RC.CO)
description: Coordinating communication with stakeholders during recovery activities.

title: Goal is returning to operations within RTO/RPO from BIA
description: Recovery aims to return the organization to normal operations within the RTO/RPO thresholds defined in the Business Impact Analysis.

title: Authority
description: One of the three classification axes; concerns the source or basis of a framework's authority.

title: Structure
description: One of the three classification axes; concerns the structural form of a framework.

title: Intent
description: One of the three classification axes; concerns the purpose or intent of a framework.

title: Voluntary
description: Authority value: the framework is adopted voluntarily, without a binding obligation.

title: Certifiable
description: Authority value: the framework supports formal certification by an accredited body.

title: Outcomes
description: Structure value: the framework is organized around desired outcomes rather than specific rules.

title: Requirements
description: Structure value: the framework is organized around explicit requirements to be satisfied.

title: Common language
description: Intent value: the framework's purpose is to provide a common language across stakeholders.

title: Management system
description: Intent value: the framework's purpose is to define a management system that runs the security function.

title: Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities (GV.RR)
description: Establishing and communicating cybersecurity roles, responsibilities, and authorities to foster accountability, performance assessment, and continuous improvement.

title: Policy (GV.PO)
description: Establishing, communicating, and enforcing organizational cybersecurity policy.

title: Oversight (GV.OV)
description: Using results of organization-wide cybersecurity risk management activities and performance to inform, improve, and adjust the risk management strategy.

title: Improvement (ID.IM)
description: Identifying improvements to organizational cybersecurity risk management processes, procedures, and activities across all CSF Functions.

title: Technology Infrastructure Resilience (PR.IR)
description: Managing security architectures with the resilience properties to protect organizational asset confidentiality, integrity, and availability, and organizational resilience.

title: Incident Management (RS.MA)
description: Managing responses to detected cybersecurity incidents, including triage, validation, categorization, prioritization, escalation, and closure.

title: Incident Analysis (RS.AN)
description: Performing investigation and analysis to ensure effective response and support recovery activities, including determining incident scope, root cause, and impact.
